name: Atto
summary: Time tracking and timesheets for hourly and mobile teams. Track hours, breaks and locations with GPS and turn timesheets into payroll-ready reports.
best_for: hourly and mobile crews (construction, cleaning, field service) that want dead-simple clock-in/out, GPS-verified timesheets and payroll-ready exports
skip_if: office/knowledge teams (project-based trackers like Toggl fit better), or anywhere the team hasn't been brought along on why
honest_knock: Simple and honest pricing — the real conversation with any field-team tracker is the human one: GPS tracking of employees needs transparency and often consent (rules differ by country), and adoption dies the day the crew feels surveilled rather than served. Roll it out as 'accurate paychecks and fewer timesheet fights', involve the team, and the tool pays for itself; roll it out as surveillance and no feature list saves it.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-09-24 from the plan data behind attotime.com/pricing; amounts unchanged since 5 Sep) Per user per month, billed annually: Starter $5.65, Plus $7.95 (job codes, breaks and notes), Advanced $10.75 (job costing), Expert $16.55 (talk to sales). Billed monthly the same tiers are $6.95, $9.95, $12.95 and $19.95, so annual billing saves about 19% on Starter, 20% on Plus and 17% on Advanced and Expert. Payroll processing is an add-on at $5.95 per payroll user a month plus a $39.95 monthly base fee, with unlimited payroll runs, and is available to US-based businesses only. No base price and no setup fee on the plans themselves, unlimited jobs and locations, and a free sign-up to start: a 14-day trial without a credit card, after which nothing is charged unless you choose to subscribe. The pricing FAQ says there are no hidden charges or usage limits; the bill is the number of users. History: our earlier read put Starter at about $6.95 and the top tier at $19.95; the current ladder is lower on every rung.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 during the free trial, without a card, without any payroll, Google or Microsoft connection, without installing the app and without inviting team members: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We clocked two work sessions of about two minutes from the browser with a gap of about a minute between them, timing every click with the browser clock, and compared the timesheet with what we measured.
findings: Clocking in from the browser needed no app: the Time Clock page has a large CLOCK IN button, after which the status read 'On the Clock', location 'Web Clock In', job code Uncategorized, with options to add notes, take a break or add a job.

We measured 132.7 s and 131.5 s of work (264.2 s, 4.40 minutes) with 71.4 s not clocked in between. Reports > Timesheets for that week showed Total Paid Hours 4m and Regular 4m, with no break counted: the gap rightly stayed out of the worked time. The overview shows whole minutes, so seconds cannot be checked there.
On the day of sign-up the sidebar already said '13 days left in trial', against '14 day free trial' on the website. No card was asked.
After clocking out, 'Earlier Today' listed 9:09pm Web Clock In and 9:11pm Web Clock Out, but the Total Hours counter on the clock page jumped back to 00h 00m 00s.

Per employee the timesheet offers Edit Time Card, New Time Card and Details, with a Download button and tabs for Pay, Miles, Job Codes and Time Off. We saw no paywall on these screens during the trial, but did not edit or download anything.
not_tested: Editing a time card and whether the change can be traced (audit trail)
Downloading or exporting the timesheet, and payroll
The mobile app, GPS and geofencing, and breaks through Take Break
Rounding rules in seconds (the overview shows whole minutes)
What happens after the trial without a card
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
